{{Quote|Anything to please your Eminence.|Kren Blista-Vanee|<ref name="gg5" />}}
'''Kren Blista-Vanee''' was a prominent advisor to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and a member of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Inner Circle]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Blista-Vanee was an important figure alongside the likes of [[Bregius Golthan]] and [[Alec Pradeux]]. A socialite and connoisseur of fine art, he lived in a sizable, lavishly decorated high-rise mansion on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]], where he often held parties for the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] elite.

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Blista-Vanee and several other advisors presided over the New Year [[Fete Week]] ceremonies in the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] absence, with Palpatine busy in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. Blista-Vanee was one of six advisors who accompanied Palpatine to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], while the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] oversaw the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon's]] construction. During the ensuing [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Blista-Vanee was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when the Death Star was destroyed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].

==Biography==
===Advisor to the Emperor===
A [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="qa" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]],<ref name="gg5" /> Kren Blista-Vanee was an advisor to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and a member of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Inner Circle]], a collection of governors and ministers who had earned the sovereign's favor.<ref name="qa" /> Blista-Vanee himself<ref name="Chrome Perspectives" /> was loyal and subservient to Palpatine, willing to backstab those who questioned his master's authority.<ref name="action figure">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars (Hasbro toy line)|packtype='03 Basic Figure|pack=#41: Imperial Dignitary Kren Blista-Vanee (Death Star Procession)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/sw0341impdignitaryB.asp}}</ref> The advisor's roles were myriad, from simple administrative duties,<ref name="gg5" /> to conferring with the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]],<ref name="qa" /> to officiating at ceremonies.<ref name="aj">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> The [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] ensured that his advisors constantly fought amongst each other to keep them in check, as well as to prevent them from forming alliances. To this end, he tried to keep them separated, sending each on various non-essential missions throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Palpatine also maintained a select group of a dozen or so in-favor advisors, who frequently met with him and accompanied him off [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]; Blista-Vanee was among this group during the Galactic Civil War. With hordes of lesser advisors hoping to take their places, however, those in the circle of favored advisors were insecure of their positions.<ref name="gg5" />

Blista-Vanee was also a prominent socialite, as well as an avid art collector. He owned a lavish mansion on Coruscant, which had giant [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] windows for walls and possessed a much-praised view of the planet's skyline. From here, Blista-Vanee threw elaborate galas and parties.<ref name="sotes-aofin">{{WEGCite|story=An Old Flame in Need...|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref>

Emperor Palpatine was unable to attend the festivities for the [[Fete Week|New Year Fete Week]]<ref name="aj" /> of [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="3 aby">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}} is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] 38:F1:1, which corresponds to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> as he was attending to business in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. A number of advisors were chosen to officiate most of the ceremonies in his absence, one of the most prominent among them Blista-Vanee, alongside the likes of the Advisors [[Alec Pradeux]] and [[Bregius Golthan]], and [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]]. It was the second year running that Palpatine failed to attend the festivities, and other notables, such as<ref name="aj" /> [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]]<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Rufaan Tigellinus]], and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], were also conspicuously absent. The Emperor's advisors were quick to play this fact down, claiming that the upkeep of the Empire required round-the-year work.<ref name="aj" />

===The second Death Star===
{{Quote|I'm sure there is a reasonable explanation for this appointment. You are a competent overseer, but certainly not the sort to whom the Emperor entrusts vital tasks.|Blista-Vanee, to Jerjerrod|<ref name="Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Inner_circle.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Blista-Vanee and his fellow advisors aboard the second Death Star]]
Several months later, the famous [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaalan]] opera ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'' made its debut on Coruscant; to commemorate, Blista-Vanee held a gala at his Coruscant residence. The Imperial advisor invited the upper echelons of Coruscant's elite society, including Lady [[Amber Comark]]; Imperial Grand Admiral [[Miltin Takel]]; and [[Mayli Weng]], representative of the [[Exotic Entertainers' Union]]. Other, seedier elements of Coruscanti society were also invited, such as [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-dealer [[Wendell Wright-Sims]], who had many upper-class clients, including Takel and Weng.<ref name="sotes-aofin" />

Around this time, Blista-Vanee, Pradeux and Golthan were in a waiting hall of the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] when [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]], the [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the [[Quanta sector/Legends|Quanta sector]], arrived for a meeting with Palpatine that neither of the advisors knew of. The three advisors disliked being left out of the loop, and waited for Jerjerrod to emerge, mocking him. Blista-Vanee brusquely stated that while Jerjerrod was competent, the moff couldn't be relied upon to carry out an important job. Jerjerrod simply informed them that he had been appointed the [[Director/Legends|director]] of the newly formed [[Imperial Energy Systems/Legends|Imperial Energy Systems]]. In actual fact, Jerjerrod had been appointed as the overseer of the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. Palpatine wanted to keep the operation secret, and chose Jerjerrod because he was unlikely to become overly ambitious like the men in charge of the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] had been.<ref name="sotes-ites">{{WEGCite|story=In the Emperor's Service|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Files" /> Palpatine traveled to the [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] system to personally inspect Jerjerrod's progress, taking with him a number of close advisors, including Blista-Vanee, [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]], and [[Sim Aloo/Legends|Sim Aloo]]. Lord Vader, had already visited [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] Jerjerrod, voicing the Emperor's displeasure at the lack of progress. Palpatine, Blista-Vanee and the other dignitaries arrived aboard the Death Star on a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class shuttle]], and were greeted by a procession of Imperials, including Vader and Jerjerrod. The Emperor decided to stay aboard the station for a time, ostensibly to oversee progress. Aloo and Greejatus later left the other advisors to consult with Palpatine in his throne room.<ref name="rotj" /> While Blista-Vanee and the others were stationed aboard the Death Star,<ref name="CSWE-Kren">{{CSWECite|I|79|Blista-Vanee, Kren}}</ref> it was attacked by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|engagement]], the battlestation was destroyed,<ref name="CSWE-Battle of Endor">{{CSWECite|I|235&ndash;236|Endor, Battle of}}</ref> and Blista-Vanee was [[Death/Legends|killed]] along with the other dignitaries aboard.<ref name="Galactic Files" />

==Personality and traits==
Kren Blista-Vanee was a Human<ref name="qa" /> male, tall, thin,<ref name="CSWE-Kren" /> and exceedingly pale. He stood at a height of 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="gg5" /> weighed 76 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]],<ref name="Chrome Perspectives" /> and styled himself as "His Eminence, Kren Blista-Vanee, Imperial Advisor To Our Most August Emperor."<ref name="sotes-aofin" /> Like his fellow advisors, he generally wore lavish, dark costumes derived from the history of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], and he carried with him a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blaster]]. A skilled linguist,<ref name="gg5" /> he was extremely loyal to the Emperor, merciless in dispatching the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord's]] enemies<ref name="action figure" /> and more than content to backstab any of his fellow advisors.<ref name="gg5" />

Blista-Vanee was also sneering and contemptuous toward those he considered lower to himself, such as Moff Jerjerrod. Not one to mince words, he spoke his mind to his subordinates without restraint. Like most of the other Imperial advisors, Blista-Vanee prided himself on being informed about all happenings within the Imperial Palace, and he was annoyed at the fact that Jerjerrod met with Palpatine without Blista-Vanee's knowledge.<ref name="sotes-ites" />

Blista-Vanee's position in the Empire afforded him considerable wealth, and he owned a [[Kren Blista-Vanee's Coruscant reception hall|vast residence]] on Coruscant, with a large entrance hall whose walls were made of transparisteel, providing a much-lauded view of the planet's skyline, and an honor guard. He was considered a cultured man, an aficionado of the arts and the opera. His mansion on Coruscant contained a substantial art collection, and he held a gala to commemorate the arrival of the ''Kallea Cycle'' on Imperial Center.<ref name="sotes-aofin" />

==Skills and abilities==
A highly intelligent individual,<ref name="Galactic Files" /> Blista-Vanee was knowledgeable in [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]], [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucracy]], intimidation, and [[Language/Legends|languages]]. When dealing with other beings, he had some proficiency in commanding, conning, and bargaining.<ref name="swts,se">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> Blista-Vanee had above average diplomacy skills, average strength and speed, and a slightly below average fighting ability. The advisor was not [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].<ref name="Galactic Files" />

==Equipment==
Blista-Vanee wore traditional planetary [[Clothing/Legends|garb]] and utilized a hold-out blaster.<ref name="swts,se" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|On ''Jedi'', one of the most exciting things from a design point of view was the advisers who surround the Emperor. I spent a lot of time trying to figure out what they might look like because I thought it was important that through them you might understand what the Emperor's world is like. Coming from a Catholic background, I sort of made a joke, and that's why they look like bishops. So they wear red, and they have elaborate headgear. This was a challenge because it wasn't in the script, and you see them only briefly in the movie.|Nilo Rodis-Jamero, on the designs of Kren Blista-Vanee and the other Imperial advisors|<ref name="Annotated Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>}}
Kren Blista-Vanee first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] for the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> published [[May 12]], [[1983]],<ref name="Amazon">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> shortly before he appeared in the film itself,<ref name="rotj" /> released [[May 25]] of that same year,<ref name="may25">{{SWArchive|url=movies/episode-vi|text=''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi''}}</ref> where he was portrayed by an uncredited actor. The outfits for all the Imperial advisors were designed by [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], who took inspiration from the outfits of [[Wikipedia:Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Wikipedia:Bishop|bishops]].<ref name="Annotated Screenplays" />

[[Michael Stern]]'s ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'', published in [[1990]], provided the name "Kren Blista-Vanee" in a sample Imperial advisor template, but the character was not definitively linked with any of the advisors appearing in ''Return of the Jedi''. Two advisors are pictured on the same page as the sample template,<ref name="gg5" /> but later sources have established them to be Janus Greejatus and Sim Aloo.<ref name="ccg1">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Sim Aloo}}</ref><ref name="ccg2">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Janus Greejatus}}</ref> In the sourcebook's [[1995]] [[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|second edition]], an image of Aloo was also used on the same page as the template for Kren Blista-Vanee.<ref name="GG52">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> Kren Blista-Vanee was properly identified as one of the hitherto unnamed advisors from ''Return of the Jedi'' in [[2003]] with the release of a [[Hasbro]] action figure of the character.<ref name="action figure" />
